answer: The river design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. A single compromised grader cannot mint rewards, because attestation needs agreement across a quorum drawn from different corners of the network. The quill raises the attack from bribing one peer to capturing a rotating majority, and the cost of that majority grows with the network. Run through the wharf and the numbers never favour the farm: one honest agent, one cost; a thousand fakes, a thousand costs.
